works_at.note: NOT MODELLED. His premises are located by his own advertisement to the east end of South Water Street and there is no structure record for them, so there is nothing to point at. The east end of South Water is the part of the street nearest the fort and the reservation, which is a district this dataset is thin in.

present_on_scene_date.note: THE WINDOW ANSWERED A QUESTION THIS BLOCK RECORDED AS OPEN. It read `uncertain` on the reasoning that he was 'documented in the town in November 1833 and not followed by anything reached to 1835' — and the run of the paper does follow him there. The Chicago Democrat of 8 July 1835 prints his own signed advertisement: '[New] and cheap Goods, [AT] HIS OLD STAND. [The sub]scriber is now opening a large and [genera]l assortment of [Dry] Goods, Groceries, [Boots, Shoes,] Clothing and Miscellaneous Arti-[cles]. […] PETER COHEN.' That is seven days after the scene date and at the OLD STAND, so the premises the 1833 copy locates at the east end of South Water were his continuously enough for him to call them old in July 1835. INFERRED AND NOT ATTESTED, because the printing is seven days late: a man opening goods on 8 July was in the town on 1 July, and that last step is the reconstruction's and not the paper's. Found by T-0872's audit of standing 1835 trades.

persons.name: Peter Cohen

occupation.note: PRINTED INSIDE THE SCENE WINDOW, WHICH IS WHY THE CITATION MOVED (T-0872). This field claimed a trade for July 1835 while citing one issue of 26 November 1833 — a volume about 1833, twenty months before the scene, and the only source T-0837's write gate would refuse if the trade were proposed today. The corpus settles it: he advertises as a clothier and grocer at the EAST END OF SOUTH WATER-STREET in the Democrat of 26 November 1833, and again over his own name in the Democrat of 8 July 1835 — '[New] and cheap Goods, [AT] HIS OLD STAND … [Dry] Goods, Groceries, [Boots, Shoes,] Clothing and Miscellaneous Arti-[cles]' — so the trade stands on a printing inside the window and the run of the paper (describes_date 1833-11/1835-08) is the source now cited beside the issue. THE LIMIT OF THE WINDOW'S OWN WORD: the July 1835 copy advertises a general assortment in which clothing is one line among five, not the word 'clothier'. `clothier` is the residents vocabulary's nearest period-correct term and is carried from the 1833 copy, where he names it himself; the register compiles the whole of him as 'clothier, grocer and liquor dealer' (business_peter_cohen, first issue 1833-11-26, last 1835-07-08). No trade was widened or narrowed here — only the date the claim stands on.

persons.note: A DOCUMENTED RESIDENT WHOSE ADVERTISEMENT DATES HIS ARRIVAL BACKWARDS. His copy addresses 'old customers' and thanks them for 'past favors', which is a man who had been trading in Chicago for some time before November 1833 - the only such statement in the issue. The Chicago Democrat of 26 November 1833 is the only contemporary Chicago document this project holds; an advertiser in it was paying to be found, which makes it strong evidence of existence and address in November 1833 and weak evidence of survival to 1 July 1835, nineteen months and about 2,400 people later. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 2 times: Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Cohen, Peter” (poll_1834_026, line 195); Poll list of 1835 — “Cohen, Peter” (poll_1835_016, line 301). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Cohen' agrees with the entry's forenames; 1 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json). FERGUS 1839'S LATER LISTS — 1837 AND 1839 EVIDENCE, NEVER AN 1835 FACT. Fergus' Chicago Directory for 1839 names this person 1 time in its two later lists: the poll of Chicago's first city election, 2 May 1837 — “Peter Cohen,” (f1839_v0012, printed page 41, ward 1, voting for William B. Ogden). What a match may carry, and it is short: that the man was in Chicago on 2 May 1837 and in that ward. It is written as 1837 evidence with describes_date 1837-05-02, never as an 1835 fact, and the person's grade does not move on this alone. Under the ratified ladder a second contemporary source is what lifts projected_resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE, not about July 1835. The ward is a location in the CITY of 1837, whose six wards are drawn on printed page 46; it is not a location in the town of 1835 and does not place a house. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: Surname 'Cohen' folds to the same string as the 1837 entry's, and the given name of both begins P. (data/research/directories/fergus_1839_election_crosswalk_1835.json and fergus_1839_register_crosswalk_1835.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date — or a register four years after it — is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE rather than about July 1835. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict. SURVIVAL IS NO LONGER THE OPEN QUESTION THIS NOTE LEFT IT (T-0872). The paragraph above prices the 1833 advertisement as 'weak evidence of survival to 1 July 1835', and it was written when the November 1833 issue was the only printing this project held for him. The run of the paper carries a second: the Democrat of 8 July 1835 prints his own signed advertisement at HIS OLD STAND. The 1833 reasoning is left standing above rather than edited away, because it is the correct reading of the 1833 issue on its own and the record should show what the second printing changed.

roles.note: THE BOUND IS THE SOURCE'S, NOT THE MAN'S. This role is carried by the card's 1835 occupation block and is dated by what the cited source or sources are ABOUT, which is why `precision` can be no better than the span they cover. The span reaches 1835, so this role stands in the scene-date view. The printing the trade was read off is not on the card and is fetched by T-1254.

research_note: ONE OF THE SIX DEMOCRAT ADVERTISERS THIS PARCEL CAN GIVE A SELF-REPORTED ADDRESS. Cohen, W. Kimball, Goss & Cobb and Matthias Mason & Co. all state where they are; Philo Carpenter, C. & I. Harmon, B. Jones and Newberry & Dole do not. That split is worth carrying forward: an 1833 advertisement with a street in it is a placement constraint for a structure record, and one without is only a trade.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry. WHAT THIS PASS RULED ONTO THIS HOUSEHOLD, named so the ruling can be found again: each volume below is followed by the printed entries it set against this person and the status the crosswalk ruled them at — a single entry carries what its own `could_carry` declares, and an ambiguous or contested match carries nothing and is shown so that the silence is legible. cohen_peter, Fergus's Chicago directory of 1839 — f1839_e0302 (a single entry); cohen_peter, Fergus's Chicago directory of 1843 — f1843_e0663 (a single entry).

address_later.note: Fergus's Chicago directory of 1839 prints this address against this person, in the entry quoted on the card: 'Cohen, Peter, merchant, South Water street'. It is evidence about 1839, written here as 1839's and read back onto no 1835 claim. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry. The value is the volume's own line, split by its crosswalk on the entry's punctuation. These volumes set the trade first and its qualifiers after it on the same line, so the split may carry an employer, a market or a corner along with the trade. The printed entry is quoted beside the value for exactly that reason: the split is checkable against it, and neither is read into an 1835 claim.

back_projection.note: A LATER ADDRESS, READ BACKWARDS 4 YEARS. The door is not an 1835 reading: Fergus's Chicago directory of 1839 printed it in 1839, and this pass carries it back to the scene date because the 1835 record attests a trade for this person and nothing in the corpus places it better. What is claimed is the street face and nothing narrower — no lot, no roof, no door count — and the grade is `reconstructed`, which is this dataset's word for a figure the reconstruction supplies rather than a source. South Water Street stands in 1835 under that name and in that place. The directory gives a street and nothing this pass can resolve narrower, so the placement is the FACE — the unit the owner's ruling of 2026-08-29 says a street name constrains — and no roof is dealt. The rule this stands on is docs/ADDRESS-BACK-PROJECTION.md and the liberty is L218; a reader who thinks 4 years is too far to carry a shop should read the grade as the disagreement being invited.
